incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Increased 5xx from ELB/control-plane anomalies in us-east-1. Severity P1. Paging @evan-t, @priya-k, @lena-b
Evan T: saw the pager. starting a triage. initial symptom: 5xx spike at 09:16 UTC, ELB target health checks showing intermittent TIMEOUT for several AZs, control-plane errors in console (504 from ELB API).
Priya K: Route53 health checks also show elevated latency to our regional healthcheck endpoints. some queries return SERVFAIL intermittently. pulling resolver traces.
Lena B: I'm on ELB/EC2 side. ELB API responses are slow (control plane). target registration/deregistration calls are timing out which causes targets to be stuck in draining or registering states.
Evan T: assigning roles: i'm incident lead, @lena-b handles ELB/control-plane, @priya-k owns DNS & routing, @marta-l handles customer comms and CS coordination
Marta L: drafting customer msg: "We're investigating elevated API errors for customers primarily in us-east-1; some requests may error. We'll share an update in 20 minutes. Incident ID INC-2026-0047." approve?
Support Team: go ahead. also pulling list of customers with >1% error increases.
Priya K: traceroute from our resolvers to us-east-1 nameservers shows packet loss on the path to specific AZ name servers. looks like DNS path intermittency not just our healthchecks failing.
Evan T: quick mitigation brainstorm: 1) shift some traffic away via Route53 weight changes 2) force-deregister unhealthy targets that are flapping to reduce reconnection storms 3) enable cross-region proxy fallback for API-kv critical endpoints 4) contact AWS for control-plane throttle investigation
Lena B: running `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:...` shows ~17 targets stuck in initial or draining state in us-east-1c and us-east-1d. control plane 504s when we try to deregister en-masse. will proceed in small batches.
Priya K: preparing a Route53 change: using weighted routing to move 75% to us-west-2 by UPSERT. TTL stays 30s for faster flip. change batch ready.
incident-bot: Route53 change submitted, change id C-2026-8899 queued
Evan T: starting target easing: deregistering problematic targets in 5-host increments to avoid control-plane backpressure.
Lena B: after first batch deregisters, target flapping reduced locally. 5xx rate dropped from 14% -> 8% in affected AZs but ELB API still reports occasional 503s when checking target state.
Marta L: customer update posted: "Traffic is being re-routed away from affected us-east-1 ELBs and we're seeing partial recovery. We'll follow up with impacted customers directly."
Support Team: telemetry shows ~9% of active customers experienced at least one failed request during peak. top affected workloads: real-time chat ingestion, webhook delivery.
Evan T: opened AWS support case #987654321 - attached ELB API traces, control-plane error logs, and vrt packet captures. AWS acknowledged and escalated to network/control-plane team.
aws-bot: Support case 987654321 accepted by AWS. Engineer ETA ~30m.
Priya K: Route53 change is at 70% global propagation. query success to our new weighted endpoints is >99% from most resolvers. Some internal resolver caches still hit the old weights; TTL 30s should clear soon.
Lena B: continuing with controlled host removals. p95 for clients in region dropped from 1.6s -> 780ms after shift but p99 still elevated for a subset of paths.
Marta L: drafting direct outreach to top 8 customers who saw >5% error uplift. CS is preparing mitigation steps they can take client-side (retry backoff, failover configs).
Evan T: adding defensive runbook change: reduce ELB control-plane call fanout (stagger registration retries) and add exponential jitter. also doc to avoid mass deregister/register storms in event of 504s.
Priya K: DNS logs show intermittent SERVFAILs correlated with times of high ELB control-plane retries - possible correlated amplification causing resolver path issues. saving logs to s3://redwood-incident-logs/INC-2026-0047/route53-resolver.log
Lena B: saving ELB target-state snapshots + instance syslogs to s3://redwood-incident-logs/INC-2026-0047/elb-snapshots.log
incident-bot: On-call handover recorded. Next on-call: @lena-b for the 2-hour watch starting 09:40 UTC
Marta L: handoff accepted. I'll keep customer comms and coordinate with CS. next update in 30 minutes or on material change.
Evan T: summary so far for postmortem: timeline, changes applied (Route53 weighted shift, staggered deregistrations), customer impact (~9% impacted, peak 14% regional error), RCA hypothesis (ELB control-plane throttling + DNS resolver path intermittency), AWS case #987654321. I'll open INC ticket and attach artifacts.
Support Team: internal tracker updated with affected customers and follow-up actions for each.
aws-bot: AWS provided initial feedback: control-plane throttles observed during high API fanout; they are investigating backend service nodes in us-east-1.
Priya K: keeping DNS monitoring on. query error rate is <1% now from public resolvers; internal resolver traces still showing occasional spikes.
Lena B: continuing to watch target states and avoid mass operations that might re-trigger control-plane issues. if AWS confirms control-plane instability, we'll coordinate sustained traffic shift and adjust runbooks accordingly.
Marta L: prepping post-incident customer summary with timeline and mitigation steps. will include suggested customer-side retries and configuration recommendations.
Evan T: thanks all. handoff notes: @lena-b takes watch, @priya-k watches DNS, @marta-l handles comms. I'll be reachable for escalation. Good job moving quickly on the weighted failover and controlled deregistration. :thumbsup:
